cohort_dimensions.label: Operational load
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Composite of workload index, 14-day overtime and consecutive shifts worked, the operational levers Welo can act on with rostering.

cohort_dimensions.label: Fatigue / burnout band
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Composite fatigue & burnout score band, the single strongest driver in the model.

cohort_dimensions.label: Age band
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Age cohort. Metabolic and chronic-disease risk rises with age. A protected attribute: reported at a higher minimum cohort size and never available for targeting.

cohort_dimensions.label: Tenure band
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Time in service: onboarding strain vs. long-service chronic load.

cohort_dimensions.label: Lifestyle risk
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Smoking and alcohol load; together the top SHAP driver of predicted absence.

cohort_dimensions.label: Department
cohort_dimensions.blurb: Where people work, in the tenant's own department names. Comes from the tenant's data rather than the model.

measure.label: Covers, occupied rooms and service volume
measure.source: Benchmark pattern for the sector, not the tenant's data
measure.note: Demand is a benchmark pattern for the sector until the tenant's own trading data is connected. Expected absence is the model's rate for each department, spread across the calendar by a seasonal pattern. Both are illustrative.

measure.source: Synthetic trading and attendance history, generated for this tenant
measure.note: The history is synthetic until the tenant's attendance, trading and agency invoice data is connected. Cover spend is what cover cost. Lost revenue is an estimate, shown as a range: each short-staffed service is compared with fully staffed services like it. Departments whose short shifts do not show up in revenue are counted, not priced.

forecast.basis: Shifts rostered to the demand pattern, absences at the model's rate for each department (allowing the rate to be off by about 10%), simulated 400 times; each run's short shifts priced with one draw of the revenue lost per short shift from the history.

validation.note: The history is generated, so the true loss is known. This is how close the method came; on a client's data there is no true loss to compare with, and this check is not shown.
